clue.text: Shed of limited height beside terrace possessed by rich guy

indicators.note: what is possessed by someone is held within them, so this pair goes inside the rich guy

parts.note: a toff is a rich, upper-class man in British slang

indicators.note: beside places one piece right next to the other, so the two sit side by side

parts.note: H is the standard abbreviation for height, and a single letter is height at its most limited
a row of terraced houses

explanation.surface: A low garden shed is set up next to a rich man's terrace of houses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Shed' looks like the garden building but is the verb, as when shedding a coat. A toff is a British word for a posh, wealthy man.
explanation.definitionFit: To shed something is to cast it off, as a snake does its skin or a person a coat.

clue.text: False woman with sex appeal various starers will gather around

indicators.note: to gather around something is to surround it, holding it in the middle
various suggests many different forms, so these letters can be arranged in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
'it' is old slang for sex appeal, as in the 'It girl'

explanation.surface: A deceitful seductress draws a crowd of gawping men around her.
explanation.walkthrough: 'False' here means disloyal, not fake: the woman betrays a trust.
explanation.definitionFit: A traitress is a female traitor, a woman who is false to her country or friends.

clue.text: Painter being from heaven?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: the Italian Renaissance master of Urbino
second meaning: one of the archangels of the Bible

explanation.surface: A painter is so good he seems to be sent from heaven.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface praises a painter as heavenly; in fact the name belongs both to the painter and to an archangel, which the question mark hints at.
explanation.definitionFit: Raphael is both the Renaissance painter and the archangel named in the Book of Tobit.

clue.text: Craftwork in gate not quite right

indicators.note: not quite complete means the final letter is lost

parts.note: a wicket is a small gate, often set into a larger one
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A piece of ironwork on a garden gate is a little off true.
explanation.walkthrough: A wicket is a small side gate; cricket fans know the word from the stumps instead.
explanation.definitionFit: Wicker is woven work of willow or cane, used for baskets and furniture, a traditional craft.

clue.text: Initial individual filled with energy — solid type that can stand the heat

definitions.text: solid type that can stand the heat

indicators.note: something filled with an item has it stuffed inside

parts.note: the initial one is the first
one single individual
E is the symbol for energy in physics

explanation.surface: The first person on the scene is full of energy and is a sturdy type who copes under pressure.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Solid type' sounds like a dependable person who can take the heat in the kitchen, but it is a kind of rock.
explanation.definitionFit: Firestone is rock that resists great heat, used to line furnaces and hearths.

clue.text: Polish smelt maybe around home

indicators.note: around says the first word wraps itself about the next one

parts.note: a smelt is a small fish; 'maybe' marks it as one example
someone at home is in

explanation.surface: Someone polishes up metal they have smelted, near their house.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' and 'smelt' suggest metalwork, but smelt is the fish, which wraps around IN to make FINISH.
explanation.definitionFit: A finish is the final surface coat or shine on a piece of work, and to finish is to polish it off.

clue.text: Delicate paper in documentary collection

indicators.note: in places one item inside another

parts.note: a file is a collection of documents
a rag is slang for a poor-quality newspaper

explanation.surface: A flimsy sheet is tucked into a folder of records.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Delicate paper' looks like tissue, but the definition is the first word alone; rag is the slang for a downmarket newspaper.
explanation.definitionFit: Something fragile breaks easily, so it is delicate in the sense of easily damaged.

clue.text: Get into sale, first off — save pounds — fantastic bargain!

indicators.note: fantastic in its sense of fanciful and unreal signals the letters are rearranged
save means except, so the letter for pounds is held out of the mix
first off means the word's opening letter is removed

parts.note: the opening letter of sale, dropped
L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin librae

explanation.surface: A shopper's breathless advice: dive into the sale early, save money, grab a fantastic bargain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'save' and 'bargain' look like shopping words, but 'save' means except. GET INTO plus ALE (sale with its first letter off) gives ten letters; take out L and 'fantastic' rearranges the rest.
explanation.definitionFit: To bargain is to haggle over terms, which is what you do when you negotiate.

clue.text: Afflict business organisation impeding sudden progress

indicators.note: something impeding progress stands in the middle of it, blocking the way

parts.note: a surge is a sudden powerful rush forward
CO is the abbreviation for company

explanation.surface: Red tape from a company hampers a sudden burst of growth.
explanation.definitionFit: To scourge is to whip, and by extension to cause great suffering, so it is to afflict.

clue.text: Friend's beginning to fall behind in climbing challenge?

indicators.note: the word's opening letter drops from the front to the back, rotating the word

parts.note: a pal is a friend; the 's means the following beginning belongs to it

explanation.surface: A friend starts lagging behind the group on a tough climb.
explanation.walkthrough: Moving the P of PAL to the end gives ALP. The question mark flags that a mountain is only loosely a 'challenge'.
explanation.definitionFit: An alp is a high mountain, the kind of peak climbers take on as a test of skill.

clue.text: Group travelling endlessly, journey including soldier and artist

indicators.note: a word that includes another holds it inside itself
without an end means the final letter is cut off
and simply adds the next piece on after what came before

parts.note: a caravan is a company of travellers journeying together, as across a desert
a go can be a trip or turn; to go is to journey
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A band on the move takes a soldier and a painter along on its trip.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artist' looks like one more member of the travelling party, but it is the definition; GI is the usual crossword soldier.
explanation.definitionFit: Caravaggio was the Italian Baroque painter famous for dramatic light and shadow.

clue.text: Cross as wild celebrators break into empty terrace

indicators.note: the people described as wild are the ones who break in, which is what puts them inside
to break into something is to get inside it
an emptied word has lost all its insides, leaving only its first and last letters

parts.note: only the outer letters of the word survive
ravers are party-goers celebrating at a rave

explanation.surface: Someone gets angry as rowdy partygoers burst into an abandoned terrace.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cross' reads as angry, but here it is the verb meaning to go across. RAVERS go inside T...E.
explanation.definitionFit: To traverse is to pass over or travel across an area, so it is a synonym of the verb cross.

clue.text: Report of trainee being given orderly treatment

indicators.note: a report is something spoken and heard, so we want a sound and not a spelling

parts.note: an intern is a trainee, especially a junior doctor or office trainee

explanation.surface: A hospital trainee's report describes patients being handled in an orderly way.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a phrase describing things handled one after another, in sequence; spoken aloud the answer sounds just like intern.
explanation.definitionFit: Things done in turn are done in sequence, one after another, which is orderly treatment of each.

clue.text: Fitzgerald's novel lacking to some extent

indicators.note: only to some extent means just part of the phrase is used, a run of letters inside it

parts.note: the letters run across the end of the first word and the start of the second

explanation.surface: Something is somewhat missing from a novel by F. Scott Fitzgerald.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface points at F. Scott Fitzgerald and his novels; the answer is a different Fitzgerald, and 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: Ella Fitzgerald was the great American jazz singer, so her first name stands for the surname here.

clue.text: A tip for the toxophilite

parts.note: surface reading: a piece of advice for an archer; setter's reading: the pointed tip fixed on the front of each shaft an archer shoots

explanation.walkthrough: A toxophilite is a lover of archery. 'Tip' reads as advice, but it means the point at the front of the archer's missile.
explanation.definitionFit: The pointed head fitted to an archer's shaft is the business end of the weapon, its literal tip.

clue.text: Spooner's timid type dislikes people living with him

indicators.note: Spooner swapped the opening sounds of words, so the two words here exchange first letters

parts.note: a mouse is a proverbially timid person; Spooner gives it the H of the other word
hates means dislikes strongly; Spooner gives it the M of the other word

explanation.surface: Someone timid complains that the people sharing his house are the ones he dislikes.
explanation.walkthrough: "Spooner's" points to the Reverend Spooner, famous for swapping the starting sounds of words: say MOUSE HATES with the M and H sounds exchanged.
explanation.definitionFit: Housemates are the people who share a house with you, so they are the people living with him.

clue.text: Group's conventional instrument, a triangle

parts.note: a set is a group of things that belong together
a square is a conventional, old-fashioned person

explanation.surface: A traditional band's chosen instrument is the triangle.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface is about an orchestra's percussion; the triangle is the drawing kind, and 's stands for 'is'.
explanation.definitionFit: A set square is a flat right-angled triangle used as a drawing instrument for ruling lines and angles.

clue.text: Prophet nobbling medic about everything that doesn't matter

definitions.note: a describing phrase for a noun: small beer is stuff that does not matter

indicators.note: to nobble someone is to grab them, so the prophet seizes and holds the medic

parts.note: a seer foresees the future

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the medic wraps around what follows

parts.note: MB, Bachelor of Medicine, is a doctor's qualification
all means everything

explanation.surface: A prophet collars a doctor to lecture him about all the trivia in life.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Everything' looks like part of the definition but supplies a piece. Small beer, originally weak beer, is British usage for something trivial.
explanation.definitionFit: Small beer is things of little consequence, the trivial matters that do not count.

clue.text: US city the last word various actors will admit

indicators.note: to admit is to let in, so the word is taken inside
various suggests different forms, so these letters can be arranged in another order

parts.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
amen is the closing word of a prayer

explanation.surface: Several actors in an American city get the final say.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The last word' sounds like the final say in an argument, but it is the word that ends a prayer.
explanation.definitionFit: Sacramento is the state capital of California, a city in the United States.

clue.text: Something of a heart of gold that has love emptying out

indicators.note: emptying out removes the contents, leaving only the outside letters

parts.note: auric means of or containing gold, from Latin aurum
taken as written, before its middle goes

explanation.surface: A warm-hearted, generous soul has all their love drained away.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Heart of gold' reads as one kind-hearted idea, but the definition stops at 'heart'; 'of gold' is a separate wordplay piece.
explanation.definitionFit: An auricle is an atrium, one of the upper chambers of the heart, so it is part of one.

clue.text: Curse from mother having son eaten by wild animal

parts.note: ma is a familiar word for mother

indicators.note: something eaten by an animal ends up inside it

parts.note: a lion is a wild big cat
S is the abbreviation for son

explanation.surface: A mother utters a curse after her boy is devoured by a beast.
explanation.walkthrough: Malison is an old literary word for a curse, the opposite of benison, a blessing.
explanation.definitionFit: A malison is an archaic word for a curse or malediction, from the same root.

clue.text: Collection of old songs, each with divine content

indicators.note: with something as content means holding it within

parts.note: EA is the abbreviation for each
DD, Doctor of Divinity, is the degree of a divine, a clergyman

explanation.surface: An anthology of old hymns, each one full of religious material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Divine' looks like an adjective for the songs, but it is a noun: a divine is a cleric, holder of a DD.
explanation.definitionFit: The Edda is a medieval Icelandic collection of Old Norse mythological and heroic poems.

clue.text: Party worker given inner room for sleeping

indicators.note: giving something an inner part puts it inside

parts.note: a do is a party
an ant is the classic worker insect
RM is the abbreviation for room

explanation.surface: A party official is assigned a back room to sleep in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Room for sleeping' looks like a dormitory, but the definition is only the last two words.
explanation.definitionFit: A dormant creature is asleep or inactive, so dormant describes something in its sleeping state.

clue.text: Tree plantations in land in very good area

indicators.note: in tells us the land word sits inside the other two pieces

parts.note: PI, short for pious, is crossword shorthand for very good
to land a fish is to net it

explanation.surface: Plantations of trees are found in land in a very good area.
explanation.walkthrough: 'land' looks like a noun beside plantations, but it is the verb, as in landing a fish, and it goes between PI and A.
explanation.definitionFit: Pinetum is a plantation or collection of pine trees; pineta is its Latin plural.

clue.text: Yarn sailors tell with no beginning or end

indicators.note: without its first and last letters, only the middle remains

parts.note: a ship's crew are its sailors
taken as written, before its outer letters go

explanation.surface: Sailors spin a tall tale with no start and no finish.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Yarn' and 'sailors' suggest a sea story, but the yarn is the wool kind.
explanation.definitionFit: Crewel is a thin worsted wool used for embroidery and tapestry, so it is a kind of yarn.

clue.text: Gentleman embracing one side, then another, is to hide away

indicators.note: then means next in order, so this piece follows on at the end
to embrace is to hold within one's arms

parts.note: a squire is a country gentleman
right is one side, abbreviated R
the other side, left, abbreviated L

explanation.surface: A gentleman hugging first one side then the other is trying to hide.
explanation.walkthrough: R goes inside SQUIRE, after its R, and L is added at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: To squirrel something away is to hoard or stash it, as a squirrel buries nuts.

clue.text: Dessert food experts rolled round in mouth to get last bit of taste

indicators.note: to get here adds the next piece on at the end
in sets one piece inside another

parts.note: cheek, like mouth, means insolent talk

indicators.note: something rolled round has been turned over and runs the other way

parts.note: aces are experts

indicators.note: the last bit of a word is its final letter

parts.note: only the final letter is kept

explanation.surface: Gourmets roll a pudding around their mouths to savour the last bit of flavour.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Food experts' reads as one phrase, but 'food' belongs to the definition. Mouth and cheek both mean back-talk.
explanation.definitionFit: Cheesecake is a sweet dish of soft cheese on a biscuit base, served as a pudding.

clue.text: Period in which representatives have 50% off

indicators.note: half off means half the letters are cut away

parts.note: agents act as representatives

explanation.surface: A spell in which sales reps get half-price deals.
explanation.walkthrough: '50% off' sounds like a discount; it removes the second half of the word's six letters.
explanation.definitionFit: An age is a long stretch of history, such as the Bronze Age, so it is a period.

clue.text: Be sustained by academic money in the first place

indicators.note: this ordering phrase tells us the money piece is put first, ahead of the academic

parts.note: a fee is money paid for a service
a don is a university lecturer, especially at Oxford or Cambridge

explanation.surface: A lecturer survives on university money from the outset.
explanation.walkthrough: Though 'academic' comes first in the clue, 'in the first place' moves the money piece to the front.
explanation.definitionFit: To feed on something is to live on it as nourishment, deriving one's sustenance from it.

clue.text: Changer of script embarrassed one having to perform it?

parts.note: embarrassed people go red in the face
an actor is the one who must perform a script

explanation.surface: A writer who rewrites the script makes the actor who must deliver it blush.
explanation.walkthrough: The 'it' points back to the script, so the second piece is a cryptic description of a performer; the question mark flags that.
explanation.definitionFit: A redactor edits or revises a text for publication, someone who changes a script.
